entries.name: Desert cottontail
behaviour: shallow dirt nest scraped in grass or under a shrub
zigzags hard when flushed, freezes between bounds
multiple litters per year when rains are good

voxel_model.pattern: buff grey, rust nape

entries.notes: The little grey rabbit of the dry southern plains; its white puff of a tail is the classic field-edge view.

entries.name: Deer mouse
behaviour: sharp white belly against brown or grey back, white-based tail
climbs stems and fences, not only ground-foraging
vector of hantavirus (Sin Nombre) in the west

voxel_model.pattern: sharp two-tone countershading

entries.notes: The default mouse of the open west; if a small grey-brown shape darts across the path at dusk, it is this.

entries.name: Meadow vole
behaviour: matted grass runways link nests like tunnels laid on the surface
numbers erupt every few years with the grass
stocks nests with grass clippings above or below ground
entries.notes: The other loud half of the vole economy: flatten enough grass and the harriers and owls arrive on their own.

entries.name: House mouse
behaviour: follows humans everywhere; grain stores and walls are its native range
breeds year-round indoors, several litters a year
tiny, big-eared, nearly hairless tail
entries.notes: Deploy around barns and farmhouses; it is the reason granaries exist as a structure.

entries.name: Meadow jumping mouse
behaviour: launches itself in 1 m arcs on oversized hind feet when flushed
hibernates ~6 months, sometimes below the frost line
lives in damp grassy margins and meadow edges

voxel_model.pattern: ochre-brown with white belly and a long scaly tail

entries.notes: A little exclamation mark of a rodent; the long tail and hind-leg leap are the whole model.

entries.name: Long-tailed weasel
behaviour: mates in late summer; embryos wait, young born the next spring
white winter coat with a black-tipped tail
pours into rodent burrows after prey with a lithe tube of a body

voxel_model.pattern: countershaded, black tail tip; white in winter

entries.notes: The small-game specialist: too big for mice to ignore it, too sleek to keep out of their holes.

entries.name: Horned lark
behaviour: runs, never hops, across bare ground and short turf
male: black mask, yellow throat and little black 'horns' that erect when excited
sings a thin, high, spiralling warble from a hovering height

voxel_model.pattern: black mask and breast band, yellow throat

entries.notes: The only lark truly at home on open ground; paved-flat instead of perched, like the plains bird it is.

entries.name: Northern bobwhite
behaviour: whistles its own name from fence posts at dawn and dusk
winter coveys flush together in one explosive fan
nests of 10-14 eggs in a grass scrape; needs shrubby cover

voxel_model.pattern: barred rufous and white throat, male boldly marked

entries.notes: The classic quail of the old field: one line of cover left, one covey appears.

entries.name: Ring-necked pheasant
behaviour: introduced farmland bird from Asia, now everywhere on cropland
male erupts in a hammering roar of wings and iridescent copper
hen hides nests in standing grain and roadside grass

voxel_model.pattern: white neck ring, copper body, barred tail

entries.notes: The gamebird that made uncultivated strips valuable; a cock in wheat stubble is a moving jewel.

entries.name: Gray partridge
behaviour: autumn coveys of one brood plus neighbouring broods, running like grey balls
male and female pair for years, coveys led by the pair
chicks feed almost entirely on insect protein in the first weeks

voxel_model.pattern: barred flanks, chestnut rump, grey head

entries.notes: The partridge of the hedged farmland; its coveys gather like a moving mosaic of grey.

entries.name: Common quail
entries.migrates: long-distance migrant; winters in Africa and India
behaviour: almost never seen walking; flushes from grass like a tossed pebble
males call a 'wet-my-lips' whistle on warm evenings
cagebird historically netted across the Mediterranean

voxel_model.pattern: streaked buff and brown, white throat stripe

entries.notes: An open secret of cereal fields; you will hear it long before you ever see it.

entries.name: Little owl
behaviour: round white-spotted head with fierce yellow eyes, bobs up and down when agitated
daylight-active around farmsteads and stone walls
nests in cavities, barns and old walls; Minerva's owl

voxel_model.pattern: white spotting and brow lines

entries.notes: The farmstead owl of the old world; a pair by the barn door is the sign the rodents are being handled.

entries.name: Mourning dove
entries.migrates: partial migrant; northern birds move south in winter
behaviour: soft cooing loop that gives the species its name
fast, arrow-straight flight with sharp wing whistling on takeoff
both parents feed chicks on crop milk; most-harvested migratory game bird in North America

voxel_model.pattern: soft grey-brown, black-edged tail, blue eye ring

entries.notes: The sound of dusk on a wire; absurdly abundant and always the first bird the player hears.

entries.name: Common starling
behaviour: murmuration: thousands wheeling as one liquid black cloud before roosting
introduced to New York's Central Park in 1890; now ~200 million across North America
iridescent oil-slick in summer, white-flecked in fresh winter plumage

voxel_model.pattern: oil-sheen iridescence, pale speckles in winter

entries.notes: The murmuration is the whole show; one flock at dusk is worth a hundred individual bird models.

entries.name: Barn owl
behaviour: heart-shaped facial disc focuses sound onto asymmetric ears
near-silent wings; quarters low over grass on still nights
nests in barns, church towers and hayricks; leaves neat pellets of bone and fur below

voxel_model.pattern: white heart-faced front, buff-barred back

entries.notes: The rodent police of every farmyard; its screech is wrong-footed enough to scare a first-time player.

entries.name: Short-eared owl
behaviour: daylight hunter of open grassland, quartering low and loose-winged exactly like a harrier
flimsy scrape nest on open ground, no trees required
booms in courtship flight over the lek in early spring

voxel_model.pattern: heavily streaked, dark wing tips, yellow eyes

entries.notes: The day-owl of the open plain; vole years bring it, vole drought takes it away.

entries.name: Prairie falcon
entries.migrates: partial migrant; some move to lowlands in winter
behaviour: cliff-nesting falcon of arid open country, never needs a tree
tail of dark underwing linings and pale flight feathers flashes in the stoop
stoops on ground squirrels and skylarks over the shortgrass

voxel_model.pattern: sandy back, pale below with darker thighs and mustache

entries.notes: The open-country falcon: if the plains have cliffs, they have prairie falcons.

entries.name: Loggerhead shrike
entries.migrates: partial migrant; northern birds winter south
behaviour: 'butcherbird': impales uneaten prey on thorns and barbed wire to tear it later
masked face, grey back, white wing patch, black hooked bill
perch-and-pounce hunting; declining with pesticide-thinned prey

voxel_model.pattern: grey above, white below, black mask

entries.notes: A songbird that behaves like a raptor; the thorned larder it leaves behind is a readable trace.

entries.name: Dickcissel
entries.migrates: long-distance; winters in Venezuela and Colombia
behaviour: males flash yellow breasts and black bibs from tall grass perches
springs up to sing a buzzy 'dick-CISS-sel' then drops back into the grass
hurt badly by mowing during nesting; numbers crash with hay loss of prairies

voxel_model.pattern: yellow breast with black wedge, rufous shoulder

entries.notes: A grassland blackbird with a warbler's colors; its fate tracks the fate of the hayfield.

entries.name: Lark bunting
behaviour: breeding male is jet black with a snowy white wing panel, unmistakable
wanders hugely with the rain; historical flocks must have been in the tens of millions
state bird of Colorado
sounds: rich bubbly warble with buzzy trill

voxel_model.pattern: black with white wing patch; female streaked brown

entries.notes: A feathered extinguished-star effect: black bird, white wing, one bound of prairie.

entries.name: Chestnut-collared longspur
entries.migrates: short-distance; winters in the southern plains and Mexico
behaviour: prairie specialist; male shows heavy black underparts, white nape and chestnut collar
males display-flight in high arcs over grassland singing
declining steeply with native prairie conversion to cropland

voxel_model.pattern: black below, buff and chestnut collar on male

entries.notes: The dapper little longspur whose whole range is a narrowing corridor of grazed shortgrass.

entries.name: Brown-headed cowbird
entries.migrates: partial migrant; northern populations move south
behaviour: obligate brood parasite: one egg per host nest, dozens per season
followed the bison across North America; never builds a nest
female removes one host egg or chick per visit
sounds: bubbling gurgle followed by a whistle

voxel_model.pattern: glossy black with a chocolate-brown hood

entries.notes: One cowbird egg explains half the drama at the nest cameras; a plains bird travelling with bison.

entries.name: Ornate box turtle
behaviour: hinged plastron closes the shell completely like a box
the grassland box turtle: home range crisscrosses native prairie
50-year lives; roadkill and fire suppress recruitment hard

voxel_model.pattern: yellow radiating lines on a dark brown carapace

entries.notes: A living antique under the grass; every adult carries decades it paid for in droughts and burns.

entries.name: Texas horned lizard
behaviour: channels rainwater down its body into its mouth to drink
squirts a jet of blood from the corners of its eyes at predators
flattens perfectly still on open dirt, fringed scales erasing its shadow; lives on ants

voxel_model.pattern: two dark spines per side of head, pale middorsal stripe

entries.notes: The 'horny toad' of Texas lore: a walking anvil of horns that eats fire ants' cousins and outwaits everything.

entries.name: Northern leopard frog
behaviour: green or brown with neat dark spots ringed in cream like a leopard
breeds explosively in thawing ponds; thousands of eggs attached to stems
leaps a metre at a time; historically dissected in every school biology lab

voxel_model.pattern: dark spots with pale halos

entries.notes: The reference frog of North America; put it within earshot of any wet meadow in spring.

entries.name: Great Plains toad
behaviour: explosive breeder: appears in road puddles within hours of a thunderstorm
warty with dark blotches edged in pale green; prominent cranial crests
trills a bleating, sheep-like call that can last over 30 seconds

voxel_model.pattern: light-edged dark blotches

entries.notes: Whole breeding guild arrives on one storm front; the puddles are full of tadpoles by morning.

entries.name: Barred tiger salamander
behaviour: adults spend most of the year underground in rodent burrows
breeders mass-migrate to ephemeral pools on rainy nights
cannibal larvae morph with big heads and teeth when ponds crowding peaks

voxel_model.pattern: yellow bars and spots on near-black

entries.notes: The prairie's hidden giant; most of the time the player will only find it crossing roads on wet nights.

entries.name: Plains lubber grasshopper
behaviour: huge, striped, and flightless with stubby wings
defense: hissing wheeze, hind-leg raising, foul frothy spit
drought-triggered outbreaks can strip whole fields

voxel_model.pattern: orange-yellow and black longitudinal stripes

entries.notes: A walking caution stripe; the plains' own warning-coloured tank.

entries.name: Regal fritillary
behaviour: one of the largest North American butterflies; larvae eat only violets
first-instar caterpillars hibernate, emerge with the violet leaves in spring
collapsed with the tallgrass prairie; candidate for endangered listing

voxel_model.pattern: orange with black chevrons, creamy marginal spots below

entries.notes: The empress of the tallgrass: big, slow and tied to violet meadows the settlers plowed under.

entries.name: Western harvester ant
behaviour: bare cleared circle of dirt around the nest entrance, free of all plants
granaries of harvested seeds below the nest
among the most painfully stinging ants in North America

voxel_model.pattern: dark reddish-brown

entries.notes: A living bulldozer with a sting; the bare discs dot the shortgrass like miniature arenas.

entries.name: Carolina wolf spider
behaviour: a hunting spider: runs its prey down, spins no web for capture
female carries a round silk egg sac under the abdomen
after hatching, dozens of spiderlings ride a week on her back

voxel_model.pattern: pale herringbone stripes and a dark heart bar

entries.notes: The basement spider grown up and outdoors; eyes catch lamplight like a tiny wolf.

entries.name: Richardson's ground squirrel
behaviour: the 'gopher' of the Canadian prairie: colony whistlers on every field edge
hibernates ~6-8 months a year deep underground
sentries whistle unlike the chirp of the thirteen-lined; coteries defend burrows

voxel_model.pattern: centred buff-grizzled back, pale sides

entries.notes: The whistled warning of Saskatchewan; every field has one and they all watch the road.

entries.name: Eurasian hamster
behaviour: crams cheek pouches with 40+ kg of grain per burrow per season
solitary and aggressive; fights that leave dung-pile territories
collapsed across Europe with industrial agriculture; now protected in parts of the EU

voxel_model.pattern: rust above, black belly, white collar patches

entries.notes: The European hamster of the grainfields, vanishing as fast as the hedgerows did.

entries.name: Spotted ground squirrel
behaviour: small pale squirrel peppered with white spots on back and sides
spends days loafing on mounds, popping in and out of burrows
hibernates the cold months; breeds right after emergence

voxel_model.pattern: white dotting, faint lines on flanks

entries.notes: The speckled little antelope-squirrel of the southern shortgrass; freeze-and-strobing movement under the cactus.

entries.name: Ord's kangaroo rat
behaviour: bipedal ricocheting hop on huge hind legs, tail counterweight
external fur-lined cheek pouches haul seed back to the burrow
needs no free water; gets it all from dry seeds

voxel_model.pattern: white flank stripe and tail crest

entries.notes: A tiny kangaroo with saddlebags, born to outpace owls in moonlight.

entries.name: Hispid pocket mouse
behaviour: external cheek pouches balloon when loaded with seed
hispid bristle-hipped, bipedal-ish hops in bare microhabitat
loner; den in loose sandy soils with side tunnels

voxel_model.pattern: harsh dark bristles, yellowish side stripe

entries.notes: The seed-hauling mouse of the sandy southern plains; never far from a grain on the ground.

entries.name: Northern grasshopper mouse
behaviour: a mouse that hunts like a wolf: stalks and kills other mice and scorpions
performs long howling cries under the moon like a miniature wolf
immune to scorpion venom; southern fiercer than its looks

voxel_model.pattern: pale above, white below, white tail tuft-tip

entries.notes: The wolf-mouse of legend: tiny body, terror of the insect world, screams at the moon.

entries.name: West European hedgehog
behaviour: curls into a spiny ball at the slightest touch
hibernates below 10 C, waking in thaws
eats garden pests; declining in Britain and Europe from fences, roads and slug pellets

voxel_model.pattern: banded white-tipped spines

entries.notes: The garden's night shift; a hedgehog at dusk is the surest sign of a living meadow.

entries.name: Eurasian common shrew
behaviour: eats its own body weight every day or dies
emits ultrasonic clicks to echolocate prey in leaf litter
caravans: mother runs with young in a nose-to-tail train

voxel_model.pattern: tri-coloured brown above, grey-brown flanks, pale belly; red-brown teeth

entries.notes: The frenetic heartbeat under the hedge; it will starve in hours without a meal.

entries.name: Eastern mole
behaviour: swims through soil pushing up surface ridges; lawns are its galleries
star-nosed relative notwithstanding, this one is solid spade forearms
virtually blind but feels earthworm vibrations through the snout

voxel_model.pattern: velvety slate grey

entries.notes: You will never meet one on the surface; you will meet its ridge-lines and mole-hills first.
